from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Epicycle Intuition", [
            "Periodic motion combines simple circular rotations.",
            "Each circle moves at a unique frequency.",
            "Multiple circles trace out complex shapes."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "#FF00FF: Draw a complex periodic path on the background."
        path = VMobject(color="#FF00FF", stroke_width=2)
        path.set_points_smoothly([self.grid["B2"], self.grid["B5"], self.grid["E5"], self.grid["E2"], self.grid["B2"]])
        self.play(Create(path), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))

        # "#00FFFF: Fade in a single circle with a rotating vector."
        c1 = Circle(radius=1.0, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(c1, "D3")
        vector1 = Line(c1.get_center(), c1.get_right(), color="#00FFFF")
        self.play(FadeIn(c1), Create(vector1), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # "#00FF00: Add a second, smaller circle atop the first."
        c2 = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#00FF00")
        c2.move_to(c1.get_right())
        vector2 = Line(c2.get_center(), c2.point_at_angle(PI/4), color="#00FF00")
        self.play(FadeIn(c2), Create(vector2), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))

        # "#FFFF00: Add a third, even smaller circle to the chain."
        c3 = Circle(radius=0.25, color="#FFFF00")
        c3.move_to(c2.point_at_angle(PI/4))
        self.play(FadeIn(c3), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # "#FFFFFF: The resulting point traces the initial complex path."
        # Simple trace simulation
        trace = Dot(color="#FFFFFF")
        trace.move_to(c3.get_center())
        self.add(trace)
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(trace, path), run_time=3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Fourier Series: Decomposing Complexity", [
            "Periodic signals decompose into sine waves.", 
            "Harmonics create a signal's unique timbre.", 
            "More harmonics sharpen the signal's edges."
        ])
        
        # Axes for the right-side visualizations
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-PI, PI, PI/2],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            axis_config={"include_numbers": False},
            x_length=5, y_length=4
        )
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "#FF00FF: Display a smooth sine wave on the screen."
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF00FF")
        wave1 = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color="#FF00FF")
        self.play(Create(wave1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "#00FFFF: Overlay a higher-frequency sine wave."
        # "#00FF00: Add a third, even higher frequency wave component."
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        wave2 = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(3 * x), color="#00FFFF")
        self.play(Create(wave2))
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        wave3 = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.33 * np.sin(5 * x), color="#00FF00")
        self.play(Create(wave3))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "#FFFF00: Sum these waves to show a square wave shape."
        # "#FFFFFF: Highlight the sharp corners of the emerging square wave."
        sum_wave = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x) + 0.5 * np.sin(3 * x) + 0.33 * np.sin(5 * x), color="#FFFF00")
        
        self.play(Transform(VGroup(wave1, wave2, wave3), sum_wave))
        self.play(Indicate(sum_wave, color="#FFFFFF", scale_factor=1.1))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Heat diffusion is inherently a smooth process.", "Higher frequencies dissipate heat much faster.", "Fourier series model these different decay rates."]
        self.setup_layout("Connecting to the Heat Equation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define visual objects
        # Metal rod (a line)
        rod = Line(start=self.grid["D1"], end=self.grid["D6"], color=GRAY)
        
        # Temperature distribution (initial sharp spike)
        def get_dist(t=0):
            # A function that starts as a triangle and flattens
            x = np.linspace(-2.5, 2.5, 100)
            y = np.exp(-t * (x**2)) * np.exp(-abs(x)) # Simplified decay
            return x, y

        x_coords, y_coords = get_dist(0)
        coords = [np.array([val + 4, 1.5 * y + 0, 0]) for val, y in zip(x_coords, y_coords)]
        temp_curve = VMobject(color=WHITE)
        temp_curve.set_points_smoothly(coords)
        
        self.place_at_grid(rod, "D3") # Just for reference, rod is wide
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(rod), Create(temp_curve))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Gradient indicator
        grad = Arrow(start=self.grid["C3"], end=self.grid["C4"], color="#00FFFF")
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Create(grad))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Smoothing animation
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        def update_curve(mob, dt):
            # Slow evolution
            t = self.time * 0.5
            x, y = get_dist(t)
            new_coords = [np.array([val + 4, 1.5 * y + 0, 0]) for val, y in zip(x, y)]
            mob.set_points_smoothly(new_coords)
            
        temp_curve.add_updater(update_curve)
        self.wait(3)
        temp_curve.remove_updater(update_curve)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: The Circular Perspective", [
            "Heat evolution damps our circular vector components.",
            "High frequencies collapse to center quickly.",
            "Thermal equilibrium corresponds to zero energy."
        ])
        
        # Setup visualization elements
        # Circles representing frequencies
        freq1 = Circle(radius=1.0, color="#FF00FF") # Low
        freq2 = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#FF00FF") # High
        
        self.place_at_grid(freq1, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(freq2, "C5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Vectors
        vec1 = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.0, color="#FF00FF").next_to(freq1, RIGHT, buff=0)
        vec2 = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*0.5, color="#FF00FF").next_to(freq2, RIGHT, buff=0)
        
        self.add(freq1, freq2, vec1, vec2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # High freq collapse faster
        self.play(
            freq2.animate.scale(0.1),
            vec2.animate.scale(0.1),
            freq1.animate.scale(0.5),
            vec1.animate.scale(0.5),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        # Equilibrium, everything collapses
        self.play(
            FadeOut(freq1), FadeOut(freq2),
            FadeOut(vec1), FadeOut(vec2),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Application", [
            "Fourier analysis simplifies complex differential equations.",
            "Algebraic tools solve oscillation and dissipation problems.",
            "Technology utilizes these principles for signal processing."
        ])
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a signal with unwanted noise components.
        signal = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(2 * PI * x) + 0.3 * np.sin(10 * PI * x), x_range=[-1, 1], color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_in_area(signal, "A1", "B6")
        self.play(Create(signal))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Use Fourier decomposition to isolate the noise.
        noise = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.3 * np.sin(10 * PI * x), x_range=[-1, 1], color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(noise, "C1", "D6")
        self.play(Create(noise))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Visualize noise cancellation leaving a clean signal.
        clean_signal = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(2 * PI * x), x_range=[-1, 1], color="#00FF00")
        self.place_in_area(clean_signal, "E1", "F6")
        self.play(
            FadeOut(signal),
            FadeOut(noise),
            Create(clean_signal)
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: From Circles to Heat: Understanding Fourier Series

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Epicycle Intuition
sections.content: Introduce the concept that any periodic movement can be decomposed into the sum of simple circular motions (rotations at different frequencies). Use a visual of a 'Vector Drawing' style animation to show how multiple circles combined trace a complex shape.
sections.example: A robotic arm drawing a character (e.g., a cat) by adding up multiple rotating gears of different sizes and speeds.

sections.title: Fourier Series: Decomposing Complexity
sections.content: Formalize the concept: Any periodic signal can be represented as an infinite sum of sine and cosine waves. Explain this as a 'musical chord' where individual frequencies (notes) combine to create a unique 'timbre' (the function).
sections.example: Visualizing a square wave transitioning from a single smooth sine wave into a sharp-edged square as more high-frequency 'harmonics' are added.

sections.title: Connecting to the Heat Equation
sections.content: Explain that heat diffusion is inherently smooth. The Heat Equation uses the Laplacian operator, which acts like a filter. Fourier series allow us to solve this by treating each harmonic component independently; heat dissipates faster in 'sharp' (high-frequency) components.
sections.example: A metal rod heated at one end: show how the initial sharp temperature spike 'smooths out' over time, matching the decay of higher-frequency Fourier coefficients.

sections.title: Synthesis: The Circular Perspective
sections.content: Connect the circular representation back to the heat equation. Explain that time-evolution in the heat equation is equivalent to 'damping' the circular vectors. High frequencies shrink to the center faster than low frequencies.
sections.example: A 'Heat Animation' showing a temperature distribution map on a ring; as time passes, the circular harmonic 'waves' collapse toward zero, visually representing thermal equilibrium.

sections.title: Conclusion and Application
sections.content: Summarize how Fourier analysis turns differential equations (Heat Equation) into simple algebraic operations, acting as a universal tool for understanding systems oscillating or dissipating energy.
sections.example: Applying this to a futuristic device like a noise-canceling headphone, which uses these principles to 'cancel out' specific frequency components in real-time.
